additionalSurfaces.semantics: Accepted and ignored, including unknown fields; runtime logging belongs to the embedding API.
Only userLevel is consumed. Other input is ignored, not a supported interface/route configuration.
Validated by the dedicated REALITY parser when selected. Additional fields are currently ignored, not advertised as runtime features.
Dynamic domain-matcher keys map to an IP, domain alias or nonempty IP array; parser budgets and geodata expansion apply.
Dynamic u32 level keys map to POLICY_LEVEL.
Dynamic header names with string/null values and carrier-specific Host rules.
Dynamic header names with string/null Go template values; see HTTP_OUTBOUND.

Requires address, port 1..65535 and explicit XHTTP method/network. A separate bounded stream is parsed with paths remapped to downloadSettings; recursive downloads, stream-one and chaining are unsupported.

objects.notes: Value types, bounds and activation rules are enforced by the executable parser.
random, roundRobin, leastPing and leastLoad only; settings are interpreted according to the selected strategy.

Absent or null settings, or a null inboundTag, mean the empty tag. The handler never dials: it routes the connection again as if it came from an inbound with that tag, keeping its source, local address and user but no sniffed protocol or attrs, by the address the connection goes to and without routing's DNS lookups. Up to 8 loopbacks in a row; a longer chain fails the connection, where Xray-core recurses until it crashes. sniffing reads as an inbound's; enabling it is refused for now.
Absent or null settings and an absent response mean type none. The handler never dials: TCP receives the optional response and is closed; UDP datagrams are dropped.

type is required and case-insensitive: none, http (Xray's fixed HTTP 403 reply) or custom. custom sends customResponseData, standard padded base64 of at most 65,535 bytes; absent or null sends nothing. Other types ignore it. Null, empty and unknown responses fail closed, matching Xray.

At most eight servers. clientIp is an IP address every server without its own sends as the EDNS client subnet (/24 for IPv4, /96 for IPv6), as Xray-core sends it. enableParallelQuery asks every selected server at once; adjacent servers with the same policy race as a group, groups settling in order. Managed selection, cache/fallback policy and IPv4 fake IP only. hosts keys are domain rules as Xray-core reads them, plain text being the whole name; a "#N" value answers with DNS RCODE N from 0 to 15. Hosts and server URL semantics require the executable validator.
network/address/port aliases override rewrite* values. Deprecated nonIPQuery/blockTypes cannot be combined with rules.

Read as Xray-core v26.10.31 reads it. qType is a number or a comma-separated string of types and ranges; a reversed range adds no type, and a rule with no type answers every type. domain takes an array or a comma-separated string of domain rules, plain text being a substring; an empty list sets no condition. qtype and Reject are deprecated aliases with warnings; qType/qtype cannot both be non-null.

expectedIPs is an alias of expectIPs. clientIp replaces dns.clientIp for this server. domains takes an array or a comma-separated string of domain rules as Xray-core reads them, plain text being a substring. URL, address/port, query-family and domain/IP-filter combinations are checked by the parser.
IPv4 only. Positive poolSize must fit the usable pool after reserved addresses; ttl is positive.
TCP supports one tlshello fragment mask. Hysteria and XHTTP H3 support one UDP noise mask; Hysteria also supports one Salamander mask, preserving array order.
One noise and (Hysteria only) one salamander mask; type is case-insensitive.
At most 16 packets, each up to 4096 bytes; reset is an idle interval in seconds, zero sends once per carrier peer.
Xray array/str/hex/base64 packets or random length/randRange; delay follows each packet, at most 1000 ms per item and 10 seconds total.
Password is 4..=4096 UTF-8 bytes. A packetSize range with a positive upper bound selects Gecko (1 <= from <= to <= 2048); padding stops at 1452 bytes.

domainStrategy, or targetStrategy when nonempty, is deprecated and migrates to sockopt.domainStrategy, as in Xray-core. redirect is host:port as Go's SplitHostPort reads it; it replaces the destination address unless the host is empty, 0.0.0.0 or ::, and the port unless it is 0. userLevel selects the policy level of freedom's idle timer. proxyProtocol 1 or 2 writes that PROXY protocol header first; other values are ignored. finalRules are checked in order against each address freedom connects or sends to, and are ignored when freedom dials through dialerProxy. ipsBlocked is removed and ignored with a warning. noises, deprecated as in Xray-core, sends up to 16 datagrams before each UDP flow's first; the removed noise object is refused. Only the bounded tlshello fragment option is supported; other freedom settings fail closed.

type is rand, str, hex or base64, case-sensitively. packet is trimmed, and gives at most 4096 bytes: a length or range of random bytes for rand; the text itself for str; hex digits; or base64 in either alphabet, padding optional. delay is milliseconds, a number or range up to 1000. applyTo is ip (or all, or empty), ipv4 or ipv6, ignoring case.

action is allow or block, case-insensitive. network is a comma-separated string or array; names other than tcp and udp match nothing, and absent or empty matches every network. port and ip read as in routing rules, and ip may also be a comma-separated string. blockDelay is seconds, an integer or min-max, defaulting to 30-90.
Exactly one fragment mask; type is case-insensitive.
Only packets=tlshello. Positive lengths 1..16384, delays 0..1000 ms, up to 16 sequence entries, maxSplit 0..4096; actual plans cap at 4096 records and 10 seconds.
Legacy tlshello spelling. Same runtime bounds as FinalMask; interval is the delay range.
Timeout/window numbers are i32 clamped at zero. Header validity and Vision combinations also require core compilation.
Opt-in raw TCP race. tryDelayMs=0 disables it; bounds and transport combinations are validated.
acceptProxyProtocol is ignored on the client. headers must not contain Host. REALITY is unsupported.

Proxy-Authorization: Basic credentials, as Xray-core reads them: strings of any length, absent or null reading as empty; a later account replaces an earlier one with the same user. Credentials are redacted.

accounts (or users, read only when accounts is absent or null) lists at most 64 accounts, of which a request must name one; an empty list needs none. allowTransparent cannot be true. timeout is accepted for compatibility.

One flattened server or exactly one servers entry; mixing forms is rejected, while headers belongs to both. Credentials are absent (no authentication) or a user of 1..1024 bytes without `:` plus an optional pass of at most 1024 bytes, neither with control characters (RFC 7617 Basic); a lone pass is rejected and credentials are redacted. Level 0..255; email is type-checked and ignored. headers are set on each CONNECT after the credentials, so a Proxy-Authorization among them replaces theirs; a name is canonicalized, a null value is empty, and each value is a Go template that may name {{.Source}} and {{.Target}} and their .Address, .Port, .Network and .NetAddr. Other template actions, invalid names, control characters other than tabs and line breaks, more than 64 headers and values over 8 KiB are refused. CONNECT over raw/tcp with none or TLS, status 200 required: HTTP/2 when the proxy's TLS picks h2, HTTP/1.1 otherwise; TLS offers the ALPN Xray-core offers; no Mux or UDP. Without TLS the credentials travel in cleartext.
Nonempty address and nonzero port. users is absent, empty or exactly one entry.
user is required (1..1024 bytes, no `:`); pass is optional (at most 1024 bytes); neither may contain control characters; level 0..255. Email is type-checked and ignored. Credentials are redacted.
Linux transparent TCP/UDP interception only. Xray's protocol name tunnel is an alias. Firewall and policy routes remain operator-owned; no host network mutation.
followRedirect must be true; network tcp/udp/tcp,udp (default tcp). Destination rewriting and REDIRECT mode are unsupported.
Only raw/tcp with none security.
tproxy must be tproxy; optional nonnegative i32 mark also applies to source-preserving UDP replies. Requires Linux and socket privileges.

socks (alias mixed: SOCKS 5, SOCKS 4/4a CONNECT and HTTP CONNECT on one port), http and tun. Only loopback listeners unless allowUnauthenticatedLan is explicitly true. TUN settings have a separate compatibility surface.
Value types, bounds and activation rules are enforced by the executable parser.
Literal substring costs only; regexp=true is unsupported.

Enabled Mux supports VLESS, Trojan, Shadowsocks (2022 and AEAD) and VMess. TCP concurrency 0 defaults to 8; negative disables TCP. XHTTP and VLESS Vision require negative TCP concurrency because the pinned server accepts only UDP children there. XUDP concurrency 0 shares TCP, negative uses native UDP. Positive concurrency is capped at 64. UDP/443: reject (default), allow, skip. Each pool opens children on four parents with 128 lifetime children each; exhausted parents finish their children, up to 16 parents in all.
Value types, bounds and activation rules are enforced by the executable parser.

freedom (alias direct), blackhole (alias block), dns, VLESS, Trojan, Shadowsocks 2022 and AEAD, VMess AEAD, SOCKS5 (CONNECT and UDP ASSOCIATE), HTTP/1.1 CONNECT, Hysteria 2 and a bounded WireGuard client subset. sendThrough is rejected whenever present, including null. targetStrategy migrates to sockopt.domainStrategy on freedom; other outbounds accept only AsIs. First outbound is the default. Tag graph validation is a later core compilation step.
Value types, bounds and activation rules are enforced by the executable parser.
Value types, bounds and activation rules are enforced by the executable parser.
Flags are modeled for compatibility; this is not the Xray statistics service.

Legacy form with migration warning; prefer sockopt.dialerProxy. Requires nonempty tag and transportLayer=true. REALITY chains fail parsing; cycles and additional carrier constraints are validated by core compilation.

Hysteria and XHTTP H3. congestion brutal (Hysteria only: Brutal at the lower of brutalUp and the server's announced rate, else BBR), force-brutal, bbr and reno; bbrProfile standard only where BBR may run. Hysteria announces brutalDown as its receive rate. Native Quinn TLS has no ChromeParrot shaping, so disableChromeParrot must be true. disableStatelessReset only affects Xray servers; maxIncomingStreams has no effect on Hysteria. Carrier compilation checks additional bounds.
acceptProxyProtocol is ignored on the client.
type may be absent, empty or none; request and response are ignored.

log is accepted and ignored. remarks (a string) and meta (an object) are subscription labels, such as Remnawave's, which Xray-core does not read; they are type-checked and ignored. Missing/non-array inbounds and outbounds currently normalize to empty lists. Non-object JSON roots also normalize to an empty model. Parse success alone does not establish runtime usability.
AsIs, IPIfNonMatch and IPOnDemand. Ordered field rules and bounded balancers only.

Read as Xray-core v26.10.31 reads it. type is not read. A nonempty outboundTag wins over balancerTag. inboundTag, domain, domains, ip and localOS take an array or a comma-separated string; domains replaces domain when both are given. network names other than tcp and udp match nothing, and any port given sets a condition, so 0, "" or a reversed range matches no port. A rule with no condition is refused. sourceIP (or source), sourcePort, localIP and localPort match the peer and the address the connection arrived on; user matches a SOCKS account by name or regexp:. protocol matches a prefix of the sniffed protocol: http1, tls, quic, bittorrent or fakedns. attrs maps lowercased attribute names, such as an HTTP request's :method, :path and headers, to regular expressions their values must match; a pattern that does not compile is refused. Domain/geodata, port selectors and aggregate budgets are validated. localOS matches the running platform as Go's runtime.GOOS names it: darwin on macOS, ios on Apple mobile platforms, android, linux, windows.

Read as Xray-core v26.10.31 reads it, every field checked even when sniffing is off. destOverride, domainsExcluded and ipsExcluded take an array or a comma-separated string. destOverride names http, tls (or https, ssl) and quic case-insensitively; fakedns and fakedns+others are accepted, as fake IPs are turned back into domains whenever dns.fakeIp is on. A sniffed domain in domainsExcluded, or a destination IP in ipsExcluded, keeps the original destination. excludedDomains is ignored after string-array validation.

dialerProxy selects transport-layer chaining; conflicts with proxySettings and missing/self/ambiguous targets are rejected. A dedicated freedom fragment handler is inlined before TLS/REALITY. happyEyeballs bounds and activation rules are enforced by the parser. domainStrategy takes Xray-core's eleven names, ignoring case; only freedom reads it, and other outbounds accept only AsIs.

RFC 1929 credentials; user and pass are strings of at most 255 UTF-8 bytes, absent or null reading as empty, as in Xray-core. A later account replaces an earlier one of the same user. Credentials are redacted.

auth is noauth (default) or password; other values are refused, where Xray-core reads them as noauth. users is Xray-core's other name for accounts, which replaces it unless null. password requires 1..64 accounts and makes the inbound offer only RFC 1929 username/password; accounts must be empty or absent with noauth. udp false refuses UDP ASSOCIATE with REP 0x07 as Xray-core does; an absent or null udp keeps it enabled, unlike Xray-core. ip is ignored; userLevel is parsed.

One flattened server or exactly one servers entry; mixing forms is rejected. user and pass are both absent (no authentication) or both strings of 1..255 UTF-8 bytes (RFC 1929); credentials are redacted. Level 0..255; email is type-checked and ignored. TCP CONNECT only over raw/tcp with none or TLS security; no Mux or UDP. Without TLS the credentials travel in cleartext.
Nonempty address and nonzero port. users is absent, empty or exactly one entry.
user and pass are required strings of 1..255 UTF-8 bytes; level 0..255. Email is type-checked and ignored. Credentials are redacted.

method takes priority over network. raw/tcp, ws/websocket, httpupgrade, grpc, xhttp/splithttp, hysteria; security none/tls/reality. Carrier/security combinations and inactive block handling require the validator.

allowInsecure=true is rejected. fromMitm is unsupported. Fingerprints, certificate pins and name constraints use parser validation. enableSessionResumption is a boolean with no effect on a uTLS-shaped handshake, which never resumes here or in Xray-core; with fingerprint unsafe, and on QUIC, rustls resumes sessions whatever its value.

1..8 distinct peers, at most 256 total allowed-IP prefixes, up to one local address per family, MTU 1280..1420; userspace TCP and MTU-sized UDP. Optional 32-byte PSK. remoteDNS accepts up to 8 IP literals, default Cloudflare IPv4/IPv6; destination DNS runs through the tunnel with bounded TTL caching. domainStrategy is legacy address-family selection. Nonzero reserved bytes, custom streams and chaining are unsupported.

A nonzero IP/domain endpoint is required. Nonempty allowedIPs; at most 256 prefixes across all peers. Default allows both families. Longest prefix wins; identical normalized prefixes belong to the last configured peer. PSK accepts key encodings; absent, empty or all-zero means unset. Inbound user settings are unsupported.
Version 2, one server, nonzero port; requires matching Hysteria transport and TLS. No chaining.

Version 2 and bounded authentication; stock QUIC TLS/h3, default bounded BBR configuration. FinalMask Salamander, UDP noise and udpHop are supported. Other QUIC/socket overrides, fingerprints and bandwidth overrides are rejected.
Hysteria2 only: numeric or comma/range ports with bounded hop intervals and protected socket replacement. Existing streams survive hops and host rebind. XHTTP H3 rejects nonempty hopping.

Hysteria or XHTTP with exact h3 ALPN, first UDP mask: mode is any comma-separated mix of intervalLocal, intervalRemote and perConnRemote; remotePorts and remoteIPs (IPs or prefixes, drawn only within the server's family). Default interval 30 seconds, minimum 5. A remote hop also takes a fresh local socket and always changes the port.

One flattened server or exactly one servers entry; mixing forms is rejected. uot and UoTVersion are sing-box UDP-over-TCP options that Xray-core does not read; they are type-checked and ignored, and uot true warns that UDP stays native. Methods are case-insensitive. SS2022: three blake3 methods; base64 PSKs, at most 8192 encoded bytes and 8 AES identity keys. ChaCha requires one key. Oversized keys retain legacy normalization; v26.10.21 requires exact-length keys, so portable profiles must use exact lengths. AEAD: aes-128-gcm, aes-256-gcm, chacha20-poly1305 and xchacha20-poly1305 with Xray aliases (aead_*, chacha20-ietf-poly1305, xchacha20-ietf-poly1305); nonempty password via EVP_BytesToKey. none/plain and stream ciphers are rejected, as in v26.10.21.

Nonempty address, nonzero port, level 0..255. Email, uot and UoTVersion are type-checked and ignored. TCP uses streamSettings; UDP is native encrypted datagrams of at most 8192 bytes, matching the pinned peer.
AEAD only, exactly one flattened server/user or one vnext entry with one user. auto/aes-128-gcm/chacha20-poly1305; nonzero alterId rejected.
Nonempty address, nonzero port and exactly one user.
UUID, supported AEAD body cipher, zero/absent alterId; experiments accepts AuthenticatedLength and NoTerminationSignal, separated by |. Credentials are redacted.

One flattened server or exactly one servers entry; mixing forms is rejected. Password 1..4096 UTF-8 bytes. Empty/absent flow only. Verified TLS/REALITY required except private/test plaintext endpoints.
Nonempty address, nonzero port, level 0..255. Email is type-checked and ignored. Same security policy as flattened settings.
Exactly one vnext server is required.
Nonempty address, port 1..65535 and at least one UUID user. Unencrypted public-address destinations are rejected.

Runtime selects the first user. encryption defaults to none; non-none uses the bounded VLESS encryption parser. flow supports empty, xtls-rprx-vision and xtls-rprx-vision-udp443. email is ignored; security is type-checked but ignored.
acceptProxyProtocol is ignored on the client. Host headers are normalized with a deprecation warning. REALITY is unsupported.

extra replaces rather than merges outer values except host/path/mode. Nested extra is inert. downloadSettings supports an independent XHTTP stack for packet-up/stream-up only; no recursive download. scMaxConcurrentPosts is ignored with a warning; h2Params (any JSON, Xray inbound only) is ignored. Rust-only h2StreamReceiveWindow: optional integer 65535..16777216 bytes, absent/null defaults to 4194304; H2 only, connection credit unchanged.
Positive maxConnections and maxConcurrency are mutually exclusive. Ranges and default/zero semantics require parser validation.

validation.acceptance: Exactly the linked xray-config parser with the same geodata search paths. Warnings do not invalidate an input.
validation.fieldSemantics: Recognized keys include compatibility-only and restricted fields. Unknown keys fail when their grammar node is parsed. Activation, value types, aliases, cross-field constraints and budgets are enforced by the executable validator.
validation.geodata: Local files are read only when referenced; no downloads. CLI defaults match run (config directory, working directory, executable directory). --geodata-dir selects an exclusive ordered search list.
